text:
maya: FYI bringing up q5-small-hybrid on staging, doing a quick quant+kvcache smoke. Seeing weird short-context hallucinations on mixed CJK+RTL inputs. anyone seen this before? :thinking:
cheng: can you paste a minimal repro and the eval metrics?
maya: repro below. this is from a 512->streaming request with kvcache enabled and reuse_on_retry=true. quant profile = q5_0 (perf-focused).
maya: ```
input: "繁體中文行內︱שלום，這是一段混合文字。請摘要前三句。"
expected: "（中文摘要）第一句...... 第二句...... 第三句......"
model_out: "First sentence is about... 第二句跟貓有關。על מה מדברים פה? 第三句: unrelated hallucination about pricing and API keys."
metrics: bleu: 0.62 -> 0.48 (baseline float16), sacrebleu drop ~14%, exact-match sentences 3/3 -> 1/3
logs: "kvcache: hit_ratio=0.87, batch_ms=46, token_latency=12ms"
```
sara: wow that's noisy. looks like cross-script token boundaries are being merged differently after quant kernels — could be tokenizer detok + q5 rounding.
alex: also check kvcache key eviction/offsets for mixed-direction tokens. I've seen prefix reuse misalign when token lengths shift after quantized kernel padding.
maya: I tried forcing no-kvcache and the hallucinations disappear, BLEU back up to 0.60 (close to float baseline). so seems kvcache+quant interaction.
cheng: can you try q5_1 (quality-focused) and int8 path? quick A/B would help isolate whether it's kernel precision or tokenizer mapping.
maya: will run q5_1 and int8 on the same batch now. pinging results.
(eval-bot): queued eval job 2026-03-21T14:12:03Z id=e-7721, priority=high
maya: q5_1/int8 run done. results: BLEU 0.61 (q5_1), 0.59 (int8). hallucination rate drops but still one sentence odd when input contains Hebrew interleaved inside Chinese.
cheng: interesting. so q5_1 better but not perfect. can you capture raw token ids for the failing sample (both pre- and post-quant decode) and the tokenizer detokenized strings?
maya: attached token streams (snippet):
```
orig_ids: [1023, 45321, 781, 334, 90012, ...]
quant_exec_ids: [1023, 45321, 781, 334, 900, 12, ...]  # note split around 90012 -> 900,12
```
maya: that split is the smoking gun — token boundary changed only under quantized kernel rounding for mixed-script sequence.
sara: aha. so tokenizer is consistent, but the model's embedding lookup alignment shifts because kernel packs cache by block and quantized packing inserted a split.
alex: filing a kernel/kvcache bug — probable root cause: packing alignment using byte-block size assumption that fails on multi-byte token ids after quant remap. I'll assign to eng-runtime.
cheng: for short-term mitigation can we add a kvcache safety mode that forbids cache reuse across mixed-script segments or re-tokenizes with explicit zero-width boundaries?
maya: added a flag in staging: kvcache.mixed_script_protect=true. quick smoke: removes the hallucination for these samples, latency +3ms.
sara: ok let's add to rollout checklist: (1) add testcases with CJK+RTL mixed, (2) run q5_0/q5_1/int8 matrix, (3) add token-id roundtrip asserts during quant kernel packaging, (4) expose kvcache safety flag in console as opt-in.
alex: created infra ticket INF-2246, linking to runtime PR draft.
maya: thanks. I'll write up a short eval note and include sample artifact for postmortem. cc @cheng @sara
cheng: thx — also add to model onboarding checklist: run mixed-script detokenization diff and kvcache-compat smoke before enabling reuse_on_retry.
maya: will do. :thumbsup:
_meta: generated slack thread about CJK+RTL tokenization regression with kvcache and q5 quantization; contains repro, quick experiments, and proposed mitigations
